chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Rifāʿah ibn Mūsā, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who struck another man and diminished some of his breathing? By what thing is that determined?
He said: “By the hours.” So I said: And how is it by the hours?

He said: “Breath rises at dawn while it is in the right nostril of the nose; then when the hour has passed, it moves to the left nostril. So one observes the difference between your breathing and his breathing, then it is calculated, and then he is taken to account for that according to its calculation.”

key_terms.الشِّقِّ الْأَيْسَرِ: the left side or left nostril
key_terms.الشِّقِّ الْأَيْمَنِ: the right side or right nostril
key_terms.بِالسَّاعَاتِ: by the hours, meaning through timed observation
key_terms.ضَرَبَ: struck or hit, causing bodily injury

ai.seo_question: How is compensation determined in Shia fiqh for someone whose breathing is reduced after being struck?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal method for assessing injury compensation when a person’s breathing has been partially impaired by a blow. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام describes measuring the deficiency through observation of breathing over time, so that liability may be calculated proportionately. It reflects the precision of Islamic jurisprudence in safeguarding bodily rights.
